entries.scope: Diagnose and repair a QF_LRA slowdown introduced by the Boolean DAG representation change, without reintroducing the memory blowup that change fixed.

environment.notes: Release; git bisect across the 168-commit Boolean DAG branch (first-parent to the merge, then within it), plus direct A/B of the culprit against its parent.

result.culprit: 0856d8f 'Preserve shared Boolean term DAGs'; its parent c1a8288 is good.
result.mechanism: TermManager::mk_and/mk_or stopped flattening same-kind children at construction. flatten_associative_booleans replaced it but ran only BEFORE the rewriting preprocessing passes, which build fresh nodes through those same constructors and so reintroduce nesting. Localised by :preprocessing.term-size.initial being identical (28011) while term-size.final diverged (151804 -> 162106), placing the cause in preprocessing rather than parsing.
result.repair: --boolean-flatten-post-threshold, default 256 (widest node needed is 206). Restores the pre-repair clausification exactly: 110514 clauses, 98886 vars, 13788 decisions, 8.9s, 485MB.
result.memory_guard: Synthetic 20000-link `d_n = (and d_(n-1) atom)` chain reproduces the original failure: 1.88 GB peak RSS pre-repair vs 57 MB after. With the post-pass enabled it stays at 57 MB -- the pass does not fire on that shape (attempts=0).

memory_guard_verified.note: Both still time out at 180s; this is a memory result. The post-pass REDUCES memory on the very instance that motivated the DAG repair, because it removes intermediate Tseitin nodes and rewrites each reachable node once rather than materialising every prefix at construction.

result.default: 2048, not 256: 256 leaves simple-scaled200 short (20200 threshold stops), and 2048 costs nothing on the memory guard (3,346,944 KB vs 3,347,208 KB, stops 17 -> 1).

Both arms in one job on the same nodes, which is what makes the comparison free of cross-job contention. 160/160 tasks COMPLETED, 40/40 shard CSVs per arm verified (a shard killed by the wall clock vanishes silently). result.conclusion: Parity restored at division scale: identical solved count (1657), zero wrong answers, PAR2 marginally better (79,375 -> 79,215), paired median 1.002. Three of the four churn instances sit at the 300s wall. The fourth, eric.t2.c, does not and is a genuine unexplained loss unrelated to flattening -- calling it churn would have been wrong.

eric_t2c_followup.bisect: Bisected on the cluster to the same pair as the flattening regression: 0856d8f (skipped, does not build) / ba3aecc, with parent c1a8288 good at 96s. Predicate: sat within 240s.
eric_t2c_followup.mechanism_is_not_flattening: The formula is IDENTICAL across the commit -- 42,784 terms and 24,505 SAT variables on both sides -- differing only by 96 removed clauses (0.3%), which are duplicates eliminated by the per-assertion visited set added to assert_positive. The post-flattening pass fires normally (11,316 accepted, 0 threshold stops) and changing its threshold (0 / 2048 / 16384) makes no difference.
eric_t2c_followup.knife_edge: pre solves it ONLY in its default configuration (102s). Under --lra-pivoting-rule dantzig, --lra-pivoting-rule bland and --lra-least-violated-leaving it also fails at 200s, exactly as the new binary does under all four. So the old binary's success is not robust: three unrelated perturbations lose the instance too. A 0.3% clause change is simply another perturbation landing on the wrong side.
eric_t2c_followup.conclusion: Not a capability regression and not worth acting on. Re-adding duplicate clauses to recover one knife-edge file would trade a correct clausification improvement for noise, and the division is already neutral-to-positive (1657 = 1657, PAR2 79,215 < 79,375).
eric_t2c_followup.false_start: A first perturbation attempt used --cadical-option seed/restartint and looked like strong evidence of a systematic loss. It was invalid: --cadical-option seed is INERT under the external propagator (seeds 1/7/99 give identical decisions 8420 and conflicts 726), so three of five 'perturbations' perturbed nothing.

summary.bug: build_qf_lra_model (check_sat.cpp) only used assigned_atoms to pick a concrete delta rational; non-arithmetic (plain Boolean) entries never reached the printed model. Minimal repro: (declare-fun v () Real)(declare-const x Bool)(declare-fun q () Bool)(assert (or x q)) printed x=false,q=false, violating the assertion, despite the SAT search correctly deciding x=true,q=true internally (confirmed via instrumentation). Fixed by folding assigned_atoms non-arithmetic entries into build_composed_uf_lra_model, mirroring the mixed QF_UFLRA path which already folds in euf_assignments.
summary.why_fuzzing_missed_it: fuzz_external.py compares only the sat/unsat verdict, never requesting get-model. The one model-checking gate (slurm_qf_lra_model_fuzz_gate.sbatch, dolmen-based; see docs/fuzz-coverage-qf-lra.md job 119949/119950, 6000 cases 0 invalid models) uses FuzzSMT/opfuzz/typefuzz, whose predicate/UF-arity flags are documented to apply only to QF_UF* logics and are silently ignored for QF_LRA -- so it never generated a free Boolean atom mixed with arithmetic. The committed mutation seed corpus (benchmarks/seeds/qf_lra/) also declares zero Boolean symbols. Even the closest existing unit test (monotone_elimination_rejects_atom_shared_across_polarities) asserted only the sat verdict, never the model.

summary.merge_gate_on_result: 1400/1400 PASS -- 0 wrong answers, 0 reference disagreements vs z3, 0 dolmen model errors, 0 activation-missing (candidates/atoms-folded counters nonzero on every eligible shape), seed 2026081702, --monotone-elimination passed as --solver-arg.

Both confirmed to fail against the pre-fix binary (assertion abort) and pass against the fix.

results.qf_lra: Zero wrong answers either side. Solved: default 1597/1753, canonicalization-on 1617/1753 (+20, 1.1% of corpus). PAR2: default 49891.78, canon 44394.62 (-11.0%). Complementarity: gained 34 (canon solves, default times out), lost 14 (default solves, canon times out), net +20. Spot-verified three of the largest swings directly at 130s cap outside Slurm: firewire.t2.c (default timeout -> canon sat 4.02s), disj_nightmare.t2.c (default unsat 108.44s -> canon unsat 4.08s), ecoliMILPglycerolYices3-70000 (default sat 12.69s -> canon timeout) -- all reproduced exactly, confirming these are genuine, large, bidirectional search-trajectory changes, not boundary noise or measurement artifacts. Gains cluster heavily in the LassoRanker family (419 files), which the original 237-file stratified sample evidently under-weighted relative to its actual size.
results.qf_uflra: Zero wrong answers either side. Solved: default 1272/1284, canon 1272/1284 (identical). PAR2: default 3682.91, canon 3685.73 (+0.08%, noise). Zero gained/lost/disagreements.

entries.outcome: Materially different conclusion from the sample-based evaluation: at full-corpus scale, --arithmetic-atom-canonicalization is a clear net win on QF_LRA (+20 solved, -11% PAR2) and neutral on QF_UFLRA, with zero wrong answers throughout. Still not a uniform win (14 genuine losses alongside 34 genuine gains) -- the underlying mechanism (early canonicalization changes preprocessing and LRA search trajectories) is unchanged, but the net effect at full-corpus scale is substantially more positive than the sample suggested. Recorded as new evidence for docs/papers/lra-atom-canonicalization.md; whether this justifies promoting the flag (at least for pure QF_LRA) is a decision left to the user rather than made here.

results.job_127439: Answer-differential clean, but model validation found 39/45 sat cases as model-error, all falling through to validate_model.py's Real-only z3 fallback. Root cause: Dolmen's default --strict=true treats FuzzSMT's QF_LIA output (linear-but-grammar-nonconforming terms like `(* e5 e11)` with e5 a let-bound literal) as a Fatal Warning and aborts check-model before evaluating the model. Fixed with --dolmen-arg=--strict=false, now the gate's default (commit c05f24a).
results.job_127440: Same 50-case smoke shape, post-fix. Answer-differential: 48 PASS, 2 benign solver timeouts, 0 wrong answers. Model validation: 40/40 sat cases pass via Dolmen directly, 0 model-error.
results.job_127441: Full default-sized run, 4000 FuzzSMT-generated QF_LIA cases across 8 shards (7 shards exited 0; shard 4 exited 1, see below). Answer-differential aggregate: 3926 PASS, 73 benign solver timeouts, 1 UNKNOWN_INVOLVED, 0 wrong answers (zero OUR_SAT_REF_UNSAT/OUR_UNSAT_REF_SAT/REF_DISAGREEMENT/CRASH). Model validation aggregate: 3528 pass (all via Dolmen), 423 not-sat (no model expected), 48 benign solver timeouts, 1 solver-unknown. The single UNKNOWN_INVOLVED/solver-unknown case (fuzzsmt_227445__file_247.smt2) is primo honestly reporting Unknown after exhausting --lia-branch-limit on a z3-sat instance -- confirmed by its solver.stderr, which reads exactly 'QF_LIA branch-and-bound node limit reached', matching docs/qf-lia-branch-and-bound.md's documented stage-1 incompleteness, not a wrong answer or crash. That single benign case is what made shard 4 exit 1 (the gate's non_timeout_failures check did not yet whitelist solver-unknown); the gate script was updated afterward to also treat solver-unknown as benign, with a comment explaining exactly why and when that allowance would need narrowing.

entries.outcome: The QF_LIA fuzz gate (scripts/slurm_qf_lia_model_fuzz_gate.sbatch) now runs cleanly end-to-end on Slurm at its default 8x500 scale: zero wrong answers, zero crashes, zero invalid Dolmen-validated models across 4000 FuzzSMT-generated QF_LIA cases. Two real bugs were found and fixed in this session before this campaign (see the two prior commits on this branch and docs/qf-lia-branch-and-bound.md's bug write-ups); this run is the first evidence at real scale, not just local smoke testing, that stage 1 QF_LIA is sound. results.primo: gap analysis by family showed most of the solved-rate gap vs z3 was ordinary timeouts/incompleteness (branch-and-bound node limit), EXCEPT the convert family: 11 wrong `unsat` answers on `:status sat` instances, all fast (not timeouts) -- the only family with any wrong answers at all.
results.root_cause: Two soundness bugs sharing one cause: PreparedLraTheory's scale-canonicalization (item H1b) can make a compound atom's slack variable represent the original integer polynomial divided by a large non-unit scale (2^32 for convert's bit-position-weighted terms), so the slack is not itself integer-valued -- but bound_assertion()'s is_integer strict-bound tightening and gcd_inconsistent_row's free-variable-ranges-over-Z assumption both applied to it unconditionally anyway. See docs/qf-lia-branch-and-bound.md's bug 3 (under 'Where integer strictness actually gets handled') and bug 4 (under 'GCD-consistency').

entries.outcome: Found a genuine, real-world-triggered soundness bug that ~14,000+ cumulative FuzzSMT-generated cases across three separate Slurm campaigns (stages 1, 2, 3, each independently verified 'zero wrong answers') never caught -- see the fix commits and docs/qf-lia-branch-and-bound.md's 'Real-world benchmark evaluation and the fuzzing gap' section for the fix and the root-cause analysis of why fuzzing missed it.

entries.scope: docs/open-leads.md lead 12d. A fresh-eyes review of the QF_LIA code, backed by an instrumented build over a per-family sample (3 files/family, 94 files, 10s), found that solve_qf_lia_impl was discarding the Farkas-style conflict certificate LraTableau already returns and rebuilding a lemma from every arithmetic atom in the problem instead. Replaced that coarse clause with the integer stages' own derivation, via a new LiaExplanation accumulator threaded through GCD-consistency, Gomory cuts, and branch-and-bound.

results.measurement_that_motivated_it: Instrumented counters over the 94-file sample: 25,270 outer SAT rounds, 25,015 of them (99%) closed by a Gomory cut proving the assignment integer-infeasible, each blocked by a maximal-size clause. calypto/problem-001542 emitted a 219-literal clause on each of 6,528 rounds while the tableau conflict it discarded was 5 literals and the cut's antecedents were 4 bounds; convert/convert-jpg2gif-query-1141 emitted 1,266 literals on each of 19,630+ rounds against a 5-literal conflict and ~19 antecedent bounds -- 28M literals of clause in 20 seconds, and it timed out.
results.root_cause: apply_gomory_cuts collapsed a std::vector<sat::Lit> conflict to bool; gcd_inconsistent_row returned only a row id; try_branch returned only a feasibility flag. QF_LRA's check_lra_theory_in_place has always used the same tableau's conflict directly as its clause. The single obstruction was that every conflict contained exactly one sat::Lit{0}, the synthetic reason a cut threshold or branch split bound is asserted with, so the certificate could not be forwarded verbatim.
results.instance_effect: calypto/problem-001542: unsat 1.10s -> 0.02s (6,528 rounds -> 2). calypto/problem-001553: unsat 0.86s -> 0.02s. convert/convert-jpg2gif-query-1141: unknown at 60s -> unsat 0.04s (19,630+ rounds -> 6). Zero generalization fallbacks on any of them.
results.test_suite: 19/19 suites pass. New primo_lia_explanation_tests (11 cases) covers the synthetic-reason drop, dedup/ordering, per-stage antecedent recording, and the only-names-real-reasons property generalized_lia_lemma depends on. Two new end-to-end cases in qf_lia_solver_tests.cpp pin the narrowing (8-literal coarse clause vs 4-literal derivation) and that the flag changes no answers.

results.safety_design: generalized_lia_lemma() checks that every literal of the derived explanation already appears in the coarse clause and falls back otherwise. That containment test is what makes the change incapable of turning a correct answer into a wrong one: it rules out both a literal that is not blocking for the current assignment (which would fail to exclude it and spin the outer loop) and a leaked synthetic literal. An empty explanation also falls back.

results.churn_is_asymmetric: 27 of the 30 gains solve in under 5s in the generalized arm (many at 0.02s), i.e. decisive rather than boundary. 9 of the 11 losses had already taken over 45s in the coarse arm (one at 60.06s, exactly at the wall), i.e. timeout-boundary noise from a changed search trajectory. Gains are concentrated in calypto (25), the family the original instrumentation pointed at.
results.one_genuine_regression: rings_preprocessed/ring_2exp4_4vars_3ite_unsat.smt2: 0.18s coarse -> unsolved at 300s generalized, reproduced locally. Diagnosed: coarse does 995 SAT solve calls in 0.18s (~5,500 rounds/s); generalized does 814 calls in 300s (~2.7 rounds/s). The generalized arm needs FEWER rounds (the lemma is doing its logical job) but each round is roughly 2,000x more expensive. Lemma size 91 literals coarse vs 23 generalized -- on this family the coarse clause is nearly inert and propagates almost nothing, while a 23-literal clause drives heavy unit propagation and conflict analysis in CaDiCaL. A stronger lemma is not free, and on a family whose rounds are otherwise extremely cheap the tradeoff inverts.
results.complementarity: primo-generalized solves 553 files cvc5 does not, while trailing cvc5 by 514 overall (8,725 vs 9,239) -- the two are strongly complementary, relevant to open-leads.md's Complementarity section.

entries.outcome: Conflict generalization is a real but modest corpus-level win (+19 solves, PAR2 -0.18) on top of decisive per-instance wins in the family it targets. It does not close the cvc5 gap, and it is not uniformly positive: the rings regression shows that trading a long inert clause for a short propagating one costs real time when rounds are already cheap. A size-guard refinement (prefer the derived lemma only when it is substantially smaller, or when the coarse round rate is low) is the obvious follow-up, and is not attempted here.

Prompted by re-reading the paper's Section 4 (now summarized in docs/papers/arithmetic-solving-in-z3.md), which showed Primo's waterfall started at the paper's third layer.

results.why_patching_over_cubes: Cubes (Sect. 4.2) is cheaper to build and needs no tableau change, but a sampled count found 249 of 300 instances contain equality atoms. An asserted equality fixes a slack, and tightening a fixed slack in both directions makes the cube system contradictory, so cubes would be inconclusive on most rounds without also building z3's difference/octagon twist. Patching is equality-insensitive.

That matches the stage's target exactly: the full-corpus split puts Primo ahead of cvc5 by 147 on unsat and 661 behind on sat.
results.two_traps_found_by_testing_the_paper_exa: Building Bjorner & Nachmanson's own Example 3 as a test caught two things the prose leaves implicit. (1) Scoring a move by |delta| alone oscillates: with rows y = x/2 and z = x/3, the nearest fix for y moves x to 4 and breaks z, and the nearest fix for z moves it straight back. Candidates are scored globally instead -- by how many Int variables end up integral -- and only strictly improving moves are taken, which is the same monotonicity argument diversify_shared_model already makes and which also gives termination and no-worse-than-input for free. (2) Floor and ceil alone are too narrow: Example 3's answer x = 6 corresponds to y = 3, two integers above y's current 3/2, so a bounded window is searched.
results.activity: Over the 94-file sample: 310 patch sweeps, 660 variables patched, 26 rounds fully integralized, moves taken on 22 of 94 files.
results.model_validation: The failure mode for patching is a wrong MODEL, not a wrong answer, so model validation is the centre of gravity. Validated 142 corpus instances covering every file where patching moved something: 66/66 sat models confirmed, zero wrong models. That check used z3 directly rather than Dolmen, and the reason is NOT a Dolmen limitation: Dolmen does validate QF_LIA Int models, and the 39/45 model-error episode recorded in slurm_qf_lia_model_fuzz_gate.sbatch was its strict-mode grammar check rejecting FuzzSMT's (* <let-bound-literal> <compound>) terms, already fixed there with --dolmen-arg=--strict=false. What happened here is narrower: Dolmen is not installed in this development environment and make contrib-dolmen fails locally (opam exit 20), so validate_model.py fell through to its z3 Real-only fallback and reported validation-unavailable. The authoritative check remains the Slurm model fuzz gate, where Dolmen is present; the z3 check is a local stand-in, not a replacement.

Three new end-to-end cases, one of which pins the gain to patching by using lia_branch_limit = 0, where branch_and_bound provably cannot take a node.
results.tableau_change: First QF_LIA stage to touch LraTableau, deliberately and minimally: set_nonbasic_value, a narrow public wrapper over the existing private update(). Its comment carries the crux -- it is not trailed outside PivotingRule::Soi, so a move cannot be undone by pop(); safe only because solve_qf_lia_impl's lia_tableau is a per-round copy.

That was wrong and is corrected above: Dolmen handles QF_LIA fine with --strict=false, and the fallback was caused by the binary being absent locally. Commit e322af5's message carries the same wrong claim and cannot be amended after the fact.

entries.outcome: Patching is the largest single QF_LIA gain measured so far: +300 solves against a same-binary control, against +19 for stage 4's conflict generalization, and it closes 60% of the gap to cvc5 in one layer. The paper put this layer first and Primo had skipped it entirely, which is the substantive lesson -- the gap was found by reading Section 4 properly rather than by more tuning of the layers already built. Model validity is now confirmed by Dolmen at scale rather than by a local stand-in.

entries.scope: gprof profile of ten medium-hard QF_LIA instances (solved in 5-40s per the full-corpus run 128125), taken after stage 5 landed, to find where QF_LIA time actually goes. Full write-up in docs/qf-lia-profile.md.

results.build_trap: The first run used -pg -O2 -g, matching the flags already recorded in the pre-existing build-gprof* directories, and reported Rational::check_invariant as the hottest function in the program at 29.8% of self time. That function is entirely #ifndef NDEBUG and is a no-op in Release, so the result was a pure build artifact -- CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=None defines no preprocessor symbols, so NDEBUG must be passed by hand. It also inflated total runtime by 56% (153.9s vs 98.5s over the same instances). Rebuilt with -DNDEBUG before drawing any conclusion.
results.component_split: 98.5 self-seconds over ten runs: Rational/GMP arithmetic 41.0%, CaDiCaL 24.1%, LraTableau 15.2%, LRA propagator glue 10.1%, other 9.5%, and ALL QF_LIA integer stages combined 0.1%.
results.integer_reasoning_is_not_the_bottleneck: Patching, GCD-consistency, Gomory cuts, branch-and-bound and conflict generalization together account for 0.06 of 98.5 self-seconds. This independently confirms the earlier instrumented finding that 24 of 36 sampled timeouts never execute a single integer round: further work inside the integer layer cannot move these instances.
results.hot_path_is_pivot_arithmetic: Call-graph attribution: Rational::operator* has 844,353,807 calls of which 91.8% come from LraTableau::pivot and 8.0% from LraTableau::update; operator+ has 821,727,887 calls, 58.4% from pivot; operator< has 797,003,808 calls, 55.8% from bound_entails and 27.5% from update_violation_status.
results.quantified_opportunity: Rational::operator*'s small-form path runs two binary gcds per call, and gcd(x,1) is 1 by definition, so a denominator of 1 makes the corresponding gcd pure waste. Measured over the same 844,353,807 multiplies: 55.4% have BOTH denominators equal to 1, 1.4% have one, 43.2% genuinely need both. That is 56.1% of all gcd calls avoidable (947.6M of 1.69B) behind a `den_ == 1` test. The distribution is sharply bimodal per instance -- seven of ten instances are 100% both-integer, three are almost entirely fractional -- so this is a large win on integer-coefficient families and a no-op elsewhere, not a uniform speedup.
results.not_implemented: The fast path was measured, not built. Rational is used by every logic, so it needs its own verification pass (full suite, QF_LRA regression, differential fuzzing) rather than being folded into an unrelated stage.
results.correction_fast_path_does_not_pay: Challenged on whether gcd_u64(a,1) is really expensive, and the answer changed the conclusion. Building the den_==1 fast path and timing it end-to-end against unmodified Release on the same ten instances gives a median 1.03x (range 0.98-1.10x), not the ~13% the call counts imply. Three measurements explain it. (1) gcd_u64(a,1) genuinely has no early exit and costs 4.5 iterations / 9.3 ns at 8 bits rising to 32 iterations / 42 ns at 63 bits, so the premise was sound. (2) But histogramming real operand widths shows the fast path fires exactly where they are tiny: on nec-smt/prp-12-47, where 100% of multiplies are both-integer, 98.3% of numerators are 4 bits or fewer, and gcd(a,1) there is two or three iterations. On dillig/25-28, where operands are 17-24 bits and the gcd is genuinely costly, 96% of multiplies are fractional so the fast path never applies. (3) The two conditions are anti-correlated, which is the whole story: eliminating 55% of gcd CALLS removes far less than 55% of gcd WORK. Recorded as a measured and explained dead end so it is not rediscovered from the profile and retried.
results.gprof_attribution_cross_checked: Cross-checked with callgrind, which counts instructions deterministically and has no per-call mcount bias. On dillig/20-20: Rational::operator* 36.3% of instructions, operator+ 24.3%, from_int128_reduced 13.7%, LraTableau::pivot 4.6%, __divti3 (128-bit division) 4.1%. gprof's ranking was therefore right and if anything conservative; the error was in the inference from call counts to recoverable cost, not in the profile. Separately worth knowing: the -pg build is 2.3x slower than Release (34.99s vs 15.19s) and that overhead is charged per call, so gprof shares should be treated as approximate for a workload whose hot functions are called a billion times. perf was unavailable here (perf_event_paranoid = 4).
results.next_thread: Rational arithmetic is ~74% of instructions on dillig/20-20 and is dominated by the FRACTIONAL case, where the gcds are unavoidable as the code stands. The question worth asking is not how to skip gcds but why so many coefficients are fractional: scale-canonicalization divides each row by a leading coefficient, which is what manufactures them. A primitive-integer row representation would make the both-integer case common rather than exceptional. __divti3 at 4.1% is a second, smaller thread.

entries.artifacts: docs/qf-lia-profile.md; flat and call-graph profiles under the session scratchpad (not committed).
entries.outcome: The QF_LIA bottleneck on medium-hard instances is Simplex pivoting arithmetic, not integer reasoning -- the integer stages are 0.1% of self time, confirmed independently by callgrind. The obvious optimization the profile suggested (a den_==1 fast path in Rational::operator*) was built and measured at ~3%, and the reason it does not pay is itself the useful finding: the gcds it skips are cheap precisely because the operands there are tiny, while the expensive gcds sit in the fractional case where it cannot apply. Also recorded: a gprof build without -DNDEBUG produces a badly misleading profile, which the repository's existing build-gprof* flags would have reproduced.

entries.scope: gcd_u64 turned up as a hot spot in the QF_LIA profile. Rewrote it to follow GMP's structure, surveyed the literature that should have been read first, and -- prompted by the question of whether the tuning is benchmark-dependent -- measured the adversarial case, the cost of making it configurable, and the effect on QF_LRA.

results.what_changed: gcd_u64 now follows GMP 6.3.0's mpn_gcd_1/gcd_11 structure: operand swap, an early b == 1 exit placed before the trailing-zero counts, a Euclidean step gated on a 2^16 magnitude ratio, and a branchless inner loop deriving min/abs from a mask off the sign of u - v. Microbenchmark, ns/call: b==1 4-bit 6.58 -> 0.83 (7.9x), random 16-bit pair 39.55 -> 23.40 (1.7x), random 63-bit 152 -> 72 (2.1x).
results.literature_was_the_missing_step: The first pass went to GMP's source without checking the literature, which was the wrong order. The central pathology is documented: Lemire's 2013 GCD benchmark states that when one operand is 1 the naive algorithm returns immediately while the binary algorithm may need many steps, and suggests hybrid strategies for exactly that. We rediscovered it by instrumentation. The current speed record (Bernstein & Yang safegcd) does NOT apply: it buys constant time for multi-limb crypto inversion, and constant time forbids the input-dependent early exits that help us most. std::gcd is not faster than the plain textbook loop. Written up in docs/papers/word-gcd-notes.md.
results.full_corpus: Slurm 128402, all 13,306 QF_LIA files at 60s, against job 128125's primo-patched arm (rational.cpp was the only code delta): 9,027 -> 9,034 solved, PAR2 40.20 -> 40.15, 0 wrong, 0 answer disagreements, 7 gained and 0 lost. Total solve time over the 9,027 commonly-solved files 21,472s -> 21,198s (1.013x). Small but strictly positive and free.
results.distribution_dependence_is_real_and_boun: The guards were tuned on one distribution, so the obvious risk is a workload with a different shape. Measured across distributions built to make each guard dead weight: worst case is tiny 4-bit operands with neither equal to 1 and comparable magnitudes, where the shipped form is 0.92x -- an 8% loss. Every other adversarial shape is 1.01x to 1.92x. No cliff exists, because each guard is a single well-predicted compare when it does not fire.
results.runtime_configurability_rejected_on_meas: Making the algorithm selectable behind a function pointer was measured rather than argued about. gcd_u64 is static in an anonymous namespace and inlines into Rational::operator*; dispatching through a pointer prevents that and adds an indirect call, costing +175% on the tuned hot path (0.84 -> 2.32 ns) against +5% on a general 16-bit pair. Paying 175% on the hot path to hedge an 8% loss on a narrow distribution is a bad trade, and it is worst exactly where we are fastest. If it ever must vary, the mechanism should be compile-time (constexpr/template) or a cheaper guard -- runtime dispatch is the one option the measurement rules out.
results.qf_lra_checked: Rational is not QF_LIA-only, so QF_LRA was measured rather than assumed: eight instances spanning 0.01s to 58s, minimum of three runs each, original gcd vs shipped. Total 92.36s -> 92.13s (1.002x), individual ratios 0.969x to 1.198x, every answer identical. QF_LRA is neither helped nor harmed -- the win is QF_LIA-specific and the guards cost QF_LRA nothing, which is what the cheap-when-not-fired design predicts.
results.correctness: 30,251,362 pairs against std::gcd using a harness that extracts the shipped source, plus 5,160,801 more in the committed benchmark. Exhaustive over small pairs, all boundary-value combinations, and randomized across every operand width with b==1, a==b, powers of two, forced trailing zeros and exact multiples injected. Zero mismatches. 20/20 suites pass throughout.

entries.artifacts: tests/bench/word_gcd_bench.cpp (new, not in ctest -- timings are not assertions), docs/papers/word-gcd-notes.md (new), src/util/rational.cpp.
entries.outcome: A real but modest win (+7 solves, 1.3% aggregate solve time on QF_LIA, neutral on QF_LRA) from making one function match the settled practical art. The more durable output is the guard rail: the tuning is distribution-dependent, the worst case is bounded at -8%, runtime configurability is measurably the wrong hedge, and tests/bench/word_gcd_bench.cpp re-answers all of it in minutes if the workload ever changes.

entries.scope: Full audit of which Bjorner & Nachmanson techniques Primo still lacks, prompted by asking whether more remain. Sections 2 and 3 had never been audited against the implementation -- the existing paper note was written in August 2026 for a QF_LRA/QF_UFLRA-only Primo. Includes the first QF_LIA measurement of row-based bounds propagation, and of the options sandbox/paper.tex's own tuning selected.

results.sect_3_2_does_not_apply: The paper states outright that equality propagation is disabled for pure arithmetic theories, QF_LIA and QF_LRA included. So Sect. 3.2's cheap equal-variable discovery is not a QF_LIA gap at all; it matters only for QF_UFLRA, where Primo has the exact producer rather than the 2024 fast path. Recorded so it is not chased.
results.sect_3_3_never_measured_on_qf_lia: Indirect (row-based) bounds propagation is the one paper technique Primo already implements and simply leaves off (lra_row_propagation = false). It has 17 run-log entries of fuzz gates and A/Bs -- every one QF_LRA or QF_UFLRA, none QF_LIA, which is now the fragment where profiling says the bottleneck lives.
results.row_propagation_does_not_transfer: Measured on the per-family sample (94 files, 10s), six arms. Default 58 solved / PAR2 7.83. Row propagation at default caps 57 / 8.09. Row + bidirectional 58 / 7.94. Row propagation at the widened caps sandbox/paper.tex's RamParILS tuning selected for primo+ (max-row-size 256, max-fanout 1024 against defaults of 64) 57 / 8.12. --lra-model-phase 55 / 8.42. Both together 56 / 8.37. ZERO gains in any arm, 0 wrong, 0 answer disagreements. Individual losses of 1-3 could be noise; the absence of a single gain across six configurations is not.
results.tuning_is_fragment_specific: This is also a result for sandbox/paper.tex: its tuned primo+ configuration is QF_LRA-specific and does not transfer to QF_LIA. Neither lra_row_propagation nor lra_model_phase should be promoted to a global default on this evidence. Worth stating in the paper, since a tuned configuration reads as a better default unless the non-transfer is shown.
results.still_missing: Cube test (4.2, deferred behind the difference/octagon twist); extended GCD for bounded-not-fixed rows (4.3, lead 12e); CDCL-integrated branch literals (4.4, which Sect. 2 names as a deliberate design choice and Primo deliberately scoped out); and four Sect. 4.5 cut refinements -- relaxed row-integral rows (the one with measured evidence, the instrumented f_unbounded count), selection by distance to nearest integer, extremum bound deduction, and large-numeral temporary scope -- plus HNF cuts, which are large.
results.caveat_over_all_of_it: The gprof/callgrind profile puts every QF_LIA integer stage combined at 0.1% of self time, so none of the remaining Sect. 4 items can move the 4,272 unsolved files. The cost is Rational arithmetic (~41%), CaDiCaL (~24%) and Simplex (~15%). That bounds the expected value of the whole remaining list.

entries.outcome: Seven or eight paper techniques remain unimplemented, but the profile bounds what any of them can buy. The concrete finding is negative and useful: row-based bounds propagation, the one technique already built and merely disabled, does not help QF_LIA even at the caps the paper's own tuner selected -- so the QF_LRA tuning is fragment-specific and the current defaults are right for QF_LIA.

entries.scope: Pre-merge regression gate for qf-lia-branch-and-bound. Everything on the branch except three files is QF_LIA-only, but rational.cpp (gcd_u64), term_manager.cpp and preprocessing.cpp are on every logic's path, and the only QF_LRA evidence for them was eight instances. This is the full QF_LRA division, both arms, before merging to main.

environment.note: Ran locally on 14 cores rather than on SLURM: /tmp/llm2smt_slurm_ssh_config had been wiped and the cluster host/user are deliberately not recorded in the repository, so the cluster was unreachable. 40 shards, 10 concurrent, 60s timeout, 3GB address-space cap per process to match the --mem=3G the SLURM campaigns use.

results.design: Arms are the two binaries (main a004480 vs branch 5700533), not two flags -- the merge question is about the whole branch, and diffing only rational.cpp would have missed the term_manager.cpp and preprocessing.cpp deltas. Both arms run inside the same shard back to back, so a shard's two arms see identical machine load, and arm order alternates with shard parity because the first run warms the page cache for the .smt2 file and would otherwise hand the second arm a systematic head start. That control is needed locally and would not be on separate SLURM nodes.
results.headline: 1,753 files. main: 1,543 solved (936 sat, 607 unsat), PAR2 18.09. branch: 1,545 solved (938 sat, 607 unsat), PAR2 17.97. Zero wrong answers in either arm and ZERO answer disagreements between them. QF_LRA is not harmed by the merge.
results.churn_is_the_timeout_boundary: The net +2 is 10 gained and 8 lost, which is churn rather than signal -- and the churn is provably at the cutoff: every one of the 18 files sits between 34.8s and 59.2s against a 60s limit, all in LassoRanker, 2017-Heizmann-UltimateInvariantSynthesis and miplib, families dense with instances that finish just either side of the wire. No file changed answer, and nothing moved from fast to slow or the reverse.
results.timing: Over the 1,535 files both arms solve, main 6,125.2s vs branch 6,031.9s (1.0155x). Directionally consistent with the gcd_u64 work but small, and 10-way local parallelism is not a precision timing environment; the answer-agreement result is what this run is for.
results.four_bad_alloc_rows: Four LassoRanker/Ultimate files report std::bad_alloc in BOTH arms. That is the 3GB cap this run imposed, not a frontend gap and not a branch regression -- identical files, identical failure, both binaries. They are excluded from neither arm's totals in a way that could bias the comparison.
results.verdict: The one unmeasured surface named before the merge is now measured. QF_LRA is neutral-to-slightly-positive, which is what the cheap-when-not-fired design of the gcd guards predicts.

entries.outcome: Clean. Zero wrong answers, zero answer disagreements, +2 solved and PAR2 18.09 -> 17.97 over the full QF_LRA division. The branch does not regress QF_LRA and is safe to merge.

entries.scope: origin/main had moved 10 commits (the model-filtered QF_UFLRA equality producer) while qf-lia-branch-and-bound was being evaluated, so the merged tree is a combination neither side measured. This checks that the merged binary reproduces the branch's QF_LRA behaviour.

environment.note: 8 QF_LRA shards (352 files) at 60s, 8 concurrent, 3GB cap. Note the gate itself ran 10 concurrent -- see the confound below.

results.no_contradictory_answers: Zero. All 8 answer differences against the branch reference are timeout boundary crossings, where one side reports unknown: 7 files the merged binary solves that timed out before, 1 the reverse. No file changed sat to unsat or unsat to sat, and the merged binary produced no wrong answers.
results.the_gain_is_a_load_confound_not_a_result: On the overlap the merged binary solves 303 against the branch's 297 and needs 865s where the branch needed 982s. This run used 8 concurrent processes and the gate used 10, so the merged binary simply had a quieter machine. That difference is not evidence of a speedup and must not be quoted as one.
results.a_vacuous_pass_was_caught: The first attempt at this check reported ANSWER MISMATCHES: 0 while having produced zero CSV files -- the xargs wrapper spawned shells that never inherited the output directory, every shard wrote nowhere, and the wrapper still exited 0. An empty comparison looks exactly like a clean one. The rerun reports its own CSV count and failure flag in the completion line so an empty run cannot pass silently again.
results.merge_conflicts: Three, all resolved by keeping both sides: lra_tableau.cpp (model_filtered_unit_equalities and set_nonbasic_value added at the same point, independent), run-log.json (both appended; merged to 538+6+15=559), and arithmetic-solving-in-z3.md (both rewrote 'Resulting priority'; kept upstream's newer QF_UFLRA verdict beside the branch's QF_LIA half). The merge also made one of the branch's own audit rows stale -- Sect. 3.2 said Primo has the exact producer 'rather than' the 2024 fast path, and upstream now has both -- so that row was refreshed.

entries.outcome: The merge integrates cleanly: no contradictory answers, no wrong answers, 20/20 suites and lint clean on the merged tree. The apparent solve gain is a parallelism artifact, not a finding.

entries.scope: Cluster re-run of both fragments after the merge, replacing the locally-measured numbers this session had been quoting. Local runs used 8-10 concurrent solvers on one box; SLURM gives one solver per core, which is what the QF_LIA result deserved and what the QF_LRA gate had lacked.

environment.note: 60s, --mem=3G, one file at a time per task. Reference z3/cvc5 come from job 127709 on the same cluster and corpus at the same timeout, not re-run.

results.qf_lia_the_session_result_holds: Answered (sat+unsat) over all 13,306 files: dc960eb 8,704 -> pre-merge b4d3221 9,043, PAR2 43.14 -> 40.08, zero wrong. That is +339 on the cluster against the +330 measured locally, so the local box was not distorting the result -- the two environments agree to within boundary churn. The gap to cvc5 (9,239) narrows from 535 to 196.
results.the_merge_is_neutral_on_qf_lia: 9,043 -> 9,032 answered, PAR2 40.08 -> 40.16. The -11 is 16 lost and 5 gained, and every one of those 21 files finishes between 53.2s and 59.9s against a 60s limit -- the cutoff band, where 101 further both-solved files also sit. Per-file time ratio over the 2,150 files both arms solve in more than a second: median 1.001, mean 1.009, p10 0.975, p90 1.050. No systematic slowdown.
results.qf_lra_is_flat: 1,535 answered in both arms, zero contradictions, 4 gained and 4 lost, PAR2 18.92 -> 18.88, and 1.0132x on the 1,531 files both solve. This supersedes the local gate's +2/1.0155x, which was measured under 10-way parallelism.
results.reporting_trap_status_solved_over_counts: bench_qf_uf_full.py's `solved` counts status == ok, and primo exits CLEANLY with `unknown` when branch-and-bound hits its node limit: 750 such files in each QF_LIA arm (569 at dc960eb). cvc5 and z3 have zero -- their non-answers are errors/timeouts. So status-based `solved` reads 9,781 for the merged arm against cvc5's 9,239 and would invert the true standing, and the summary CSV's PAR2 charges those 750 their elapsed time rather than the 2T penalty (34.37 vs the correct 40.16). Every primo-vs-reference number in this project must be computed from sat+unsat, not from status. The numbers this session reported were already answer-based and are unaffected.
results.an_invalid_arm_was_caught_before_aggrega: The first QF_LIA submission used upstream main (2480db9) as the baseline. It reported 167 of 167 files `unsupported` per shard: QF_LIA support IS this branch, so upstream main cannot parse the division at all. Cancelled and replaced with the pre-merge branch tip, which is the control that answers the actual question. A frontend gap and a timeout look nothing alike in the data -- unsupported rows, PAR2 pinned at 2T -- but only if the rows are read rather than the totals.
results.harness_constraint_worth_recording: bench_qf_uf_full.py resolves root as (repo / args.root).resolve() and then calls path.relative_to(repo) per row, so the corpus MUST live under the repo directory; pointing PRIMO_COMPARE_ROOT at an absolute path outside it fails every task, and symlinking the corpus in does not help because .resolve() follows the link. The campaigns therefore run FROM the corpus workdirs with both arms given as absolute binary paths -- which also means no sync ever touches a corpus directory.

entries.outcome: The merge is safe on both fragments: zero wrong answers and zero contradictory answers across 15,059 files, with QF_LIA -11 and QF_LRA 0 net, both entirely inside the timeout band. The session's QF_LIA gain is confirmed at cluster scale: +339 answered, PAR2 43.14 -> 40.08.

entries.scope: Promotion test for --lra-model-phase and --monotone-elimination, both default-off, across all three arithmetic fragments at their standard timeouts. Monotone elimination was rejected in August on a 237-file 10s sample (lead 9); this is the first full-corpus reading of either flag.

environment.job: 129188-129194 (7 arms, 320 tasks); baselines are 129088 (QF_LRA), 129148 (QF_UFLRA), 128768 (QF_LIA), same binary and corpora

results.which_fragment_each_flag_can_reach: Measured before spending cluster time rather than assumed. --monotone-elimination eliminates variables on 24 of 48 sampled QF_LRA files (2,157 variables), 4 of 35 QF_UFLRA files, and 0 of 58 QF_LIA files -- it is Real-variable elimination, so a pure-Int problem has no candidates and that arm was not run. See lead 14: the QF_LIA zero is definitional, not evidence that Int has no one-sided variables.
results.qf_lra_300s_both_flags_win: 1,753 files. default 1,655 (994 sat / 661 unsat) PAR2 46.33; --lra-model-phase 1,678 PAR2 36.53; --monotone-elimination 1,668 PAR2 41.51; both 1,680 PAR2 35.14. Zero wrong answers and zero answer contradictions in every arm. At 1,680 primo would pass OpenSMT's 1,670 and lead this division.
results.the_model_phase_gain_is_mechanism_not_ch: 34 gained and 11 lost, and only 4 of the 34 finish past 85% of the limit -- these are files that now complete in 3-59s against a 300s timeout, not boundary crossings. The paired time ratio over the 576 files both arms solve in more than a second has median 0.775, with 344 files more than 10% faster against 135 more than 10% slower. That is a broad speedup, not a lucky tail.
results.the_11_losses_are_real_and_should_not_be: None of the 11 lost files were anywhere near the limit under the default: they took 9, 18, 21, 22, 22, 63, 112, 203, 220, 228 and 234 seconds and now time out. A heuristic that reorders search has genuine losers; the net is +23 and the recommendation stands, but the losses are mechanism too, not noise.
results.monotone_overturns_its_own_rejection_but: 17 gained, 4 lost, PAR2 46.33 -> 41.51. The paired median ratio is 0.999 -- exactly the neutrality lead 9 measured on the 237-file 10s sample -- so this is not a speedup; it converts a specific set of timeouts into solves without making the median instance faster. The August rejection was not wrong about the mechanism, it was wrong about the population: at 10s on 237 files the instances this helps had not yet begun to time out.
results.qf_uflra_says_no_to_model_phase: default 1,272, --lra-model-phase 1,269 (0 gained, 3 lost), --monotone-elimination 1,273 (1 gained, 0 lost), both 1,269. Model phase is 11% faster on the median non-trivial file (ratio 0.889) and still loses three instances outright. Monotone is inert here, firing on 4 of 35 sampled files.
results.qf_lia_is_a_coin_flip_with_a_bias: 13,306 files: default 9,031, --lra-model-phase 9,072, PAR2 40.17 -> 39.84. But 178 files were gained and 137 lost, and their times are the give-away: the gained files solve in under a second under model phase and time out by default, the lost ones the reverse. This flag either finds the path immediately or never on this fragment. The paired ratio on everything else is median 0.997 with 344 files faster and 344 slower -- perfectly symmetric. Net +41 against a churn of 315 is about 2.3 standard deviations under a sign test: suggestive, not decisive, and high variance either way.
results.baseline_sanity: The QF_LRA default arm reads 1,655 against the 1,657 recorded on 2026-08-07 at 300s, so the gains are measured against a normal baseline rather than a depressed one.
results.promotion_attempt_found_a_soundness_bug: Promoting --monotone-elimination to default immediately broke boolean_solver_tests.cpp's bool_argument_congruence_preserves_boolean_domain: unsat became sat. The pass is NOT at fault. That test's formula carries (assert (< 0 x)) as its only Real atom; monotone elimination discharges the one-sided x and folds the atom away, leaving a QF_UFLRA instance with no Real atom at all -- and on that path Primo's Boolean-domain bridging never runs (:no.boolean-domain.bridged-terms reads 8 with the atom present and is not emitted without it). Deleting the atom by hand reproduces the wrong answer with the flag OFF, so this is a pre-existing soundness bug on main rather than a promotion regression: primo answers sat where z3 and cvc5 answer unsat. Witness and analysis in bugs/qf-uflra-no-real-atom-boolean-domain/.

entries.outcome: Corpus evidence supports promoting --monotone-elimination on QF_LRA (+13 solved, PAR2 46.33 -> 41.51, zero wrong) and rejects promoting --lra-model-phase globally (-3 on QF_UFLRA, a 178-gained/137-lost coin flip on QF_LIA). The promotion itself is BLOCKED: flipping the default exposed the pre-existing QF_UFLRA wrong answer above, and a default that makes a latent soundness bug reachable is not shippable. Fix the bridging path, then re-promote.

entries.scope: Fix for the QF_UF wrong answer in bugs/qf-uf-boolean-argument-congruence: congruence closure was not told that Bool has exactly two elements, so it could give a Bool-sorted argument a third value. Both solver paths unified on one encoding.

environment.job: 129537/129538 (QF_UF A/B), 129539/129540 (QF_UFLRA A/B), 129713 (pre-fix QF_UF baseline), 129705 (Bool fuzz gate)

results.the_fix_is_registration_not_clauses: add_explained_theory_equality and flatten_assigned_atom already assert t = true/false into the closure for any Bool-sorted Constant theory atom, with the term's own literal as a one-literal reason. A plain Bool constant was simply never registered as an atom, so neither branch fired. register_boolean_argument_terms() registers Bool-sorted arguments of uninterpreted applications: no new SAT variable and no clause, because theory_atom_for_term reuses the literal the term already has. The older bridge encoding cost 2 atoms and 3 clauses per term and bridged Bool-VALUED applications as well, which are already atoms.
results.harness_is_the_arbiter_and_it_passed: scripts/qf_uf_boolean_fuzz.py went from 91 disagreements in 600 cases to 0, plus 0 in two further 500-case seeds. results.citation_confirmed: Section 3 describes decision recommendations. The CADE 2019 citation is verified, not inferred; the earlier caveat is removed.
results.footnote_3_corrects_the_thesis_reading: GetPhase(L) = TRUE iff the current theory assignment satisfies L OR Assert(not L) would conflict; otherwise FALSE. The footnote adds that the second disjunct is impossible when unate propagation is enabled. The thesis prose reads as two criteria and had been recorded here as 'conflict-freedom plus model-satisfaction, Primo has only the second'. That was wrong: the disjuncts are alternatives, and SPASS-SATT's default has unate propagation on, so their measured +129 comes from the model-satisfaction disjunct alone -- exactly what --lra-model-phase already implements.
results.convert_family_is_one_target: Paper: 'SPASS-SATT solves only two-thirds of the 319 instances if ONE of the following three techniques is missing: (i) recalculating simplex states during backtracking, (ii) decision recommendations, or (iii) the small CNF transformation. SPASS-SATT with all three techniques solves all instances in less than 2s.' The +117/+116/+101 figures therefore count roughly the same ~106 instances three times; each is necessary, none sufficient.
results.new_over_the_thesis: Section 4 details shared monomial lifting (-PPIL) and CITE bounding (-PPIB, one fresh integer variable per topmost CITE, bounded by the leaf min/max and gcd-scaled), which carry `rings` where CITE simplification plus compression carry `nec-smt`. Footnote 4: all preprocessing techniques except small CNF are also in CVC4, and the implementation is fast because of a shared term representation plus caching of intermediate results.
results.additional_numbers: 4894 of 6947 QF_LIA instances are solved by the simplex implementation alone; unit cube test +56 and 705 instances more than 2x faster; bounding transformations +169 and 167 instances more than 2x faster; bound refinements +24; simple rounding 1 instance faster; bound propagation +10; unate propagation no consistent benefit or drawback; pb2010 +22, all solved without branch-and-bound; nec_smt 2782 of 2800 with preprocessing (the thesis figure legend says 2772).
results.design_note: SPASS-SATT deliberately rejected splitting-on-demand, implementing branch-and-bound as a theory solver separate from the SAT solver to keep control of the branch-and-bound reasoning.

entries.interpretation: Lead 20 changes from 'implement the criterion Primo lacks' to 'A/B an existing flag on QF_LIA'. --lra-model-phase is off by default and has only been evaluated on QF_LRA, the fragment where the same source measures the technique at +11; the +129 is for QF_LIA, where solve_qf_lia_impl already wires the flag through. No new code is needed for the evaluation.

entries.scope: Diagnosis, repair, and exact-commit QF_UF model-validation gate for the invalid case-0388 model found while validating the experimental sequential Boolean-splitting tactic.

diagnosis.introduction: The defect was introduced by bcb482dda5ef3fc7f919fa88c8aa9fc373ed5b54 (Add QF_UF model printing and Dolmen validation, 2026-07-29). The minimized witness already emits an invalid model at that exact commit. Its immediate parent c495ff122e5a86a0fff130e0850188e518f1417b reports get-model as unsupported, so bcb482d is the first possible and first observed bad revision. Later preprocessing reconstruction exposed more instances but did not originate the model-closure inconsistency.
diagnosis.trigger: Solved-constant preprocessing eliminated a = tb(p), after which p no longer occurred in the final SAT problem and therefore had no explicit Boolean model assignment.
diagnosis.root_cause: The printer defaulted the unconstrained p to false, but the model congruence closure did not equate p with false. It could consequently retain tb(p) and tb(false) in different result classes even though both UF table rows printed with the same false argument key; the first row then shadowed the second and violated the asserted equality.
diagnosis.reduction: A minimal witness contains one uninterpreted sort U, p : Bool, a : U, tb : Bool -> U, (= (tb p) a), and (= (tb true) (tb false)). Disabling preprocessing or solved-constant substitution avoided the bad model, locating the interaction in reconstruction rather than the split tactic.
diagnosis.repair: Before constructing UF tables, QfUfModelBuilder now completes every unconstrained Bool constant or Bool-valued application to false inside its congruence closure and saturates again. This makes the internal quotient agree with the value later printed for each Boolean argument.

results.first_sat: The satisfiable firewire case stops after 1,1,2,3 solver calls rather than exhausting 1,2,4,8 branches; its 13,774 decisions and 4 conflicts remain unchanged and k=3 is 25% slower. The decoupled MathSAT case stops after 1,1,2,3 calls and is 46% slower at k=3.
results.search_regression: SEQ020 size 4 increases from 9,448 decisions/256 conflicts at k=0 to 14,060/581 at k=3; median time rises 71%.
results.infrastructure_cost: The split leaf itself costs at most approximately 2.1ms on the focused cases. Phase timers attribute the regressions to repeated solver setup and branch execution, not strategy dispatch or eager goal materialization.
results.correctness: All 32 focused variant/file combinations have the expected answer, with deterministic solve-call/decision/conflict totals across five repeats. At k=3, Dolmen validates all three satisfiable models and the remaining five cases are unsatisfiable; zero wrong answer, invalid model, crash, timeout, unsupported input, or disagreement occurred.

entries.efficiency_review: The focused class probe shows major search reductions but no sequential wall-time win. No repeated scan or goal-materialization bottleneck is visible; solver-leaf repetition is the intended current execution policy. The experiment remains default-off. Parallel evaluation needs per-branch timing/cost counters and isolated solver resources before these search reductions can be interpreted as speedup potential.

results.correctness: In both campaigns, each arm covered all 1,284 files and solved the identical 1,272-file set: 761 sat, 511 unsat, and 12 timeout. There were zero wrong, unsupported, error, recovery, loss, or decisive-answer-disagreement rows.
results.first_order: Specialized solved-row time/PAR2 806.958954/3686.958954 seconds; generic 823.731840/3703.731840. The apparent generic solved-time increase was 2.08%.
results.crossed_order: Specialized solved-row time/PAR2 794.175062/3674.175062 seconds; generic 781.692102/3661.692102. Reversing arm order made generic appear 1.57% faster on solved time.
results.order_effect: On the first campaign's specialized-first shards, generic was 5.23% faster; on generic-first shards it was 7.07% slower. This identifies a material cold-first-arm effect and invalidates either single campaign as a standalone timing comparison.
results.crossed_average: Per-arm averages across both orders were 800.567008 specialized versus 802.711971 generic common-solved seconds (+0.27%), and 3680.567008 versus 3682.711971 PAR2 (+0.06%). Median per-file ratio was 1.00395 and geometric-mean ratio 1.00931. Coverage and family solved counts were identical.
results.families: Averaged specialized/generic solved seconds were FFT 0.167168/0.166547, BMC 6.609708/6.584899, induction 718.873731/720.615783, and MathSAT 74.916402/75.344743. Family PAR2 differs by the same solved-time deltas because timeout sets are identical.
results.generic_activity: The generic coordinator was enabled on 1,231 solved rows and performed component checks on 755: 1,794 checks, 2,313 snapshots, 661 mutations, 142 fixed points, and 1,510 model decisions. It reported no stale/rejected snapshot, disagreement, learned clause, or fresh decision in this corpus.
results.diagnostic_difference: Search classifications and ordinary counters matched, except that 236 rows omitted specialized compatibility-projection/success counters and 225 omitted specialized compatibility-edge/already-equal counters on the generic scheduler boundary; these are expected diagnostic-path differences, not search-result changes.
results.watchlist: benchmarks/qf_uflra-generic-combination-watchlist.txt retains cs_stack_false, rtl28xxu, Problem06_60, parport, and one RandomCoupled MathSAT row. These were active generic rows with small same-direction deltas in both campaigns.
results.profile: On Problem07_00, pinned gprof wall time was 16.18 seconds generic versus 16.16 specialized and solve time 5.337/5.323 seconds; the generic path only set its enabled counter. On active cs_stack_false, generic was 17.07 seconds versus 17.27 specialized and solve time 13.005/13.166 seconds; it performed two component checks, three snapshots, and one mutation. Dominant functions were LraTableau::check, exact Rational arithmetic, LRA pivots, term hash lookup, and CaDiCaL propagation; generic coordinator functions were below gprof's 10 ms sampling resolution.

counter_results.complete_eight_row_total: Over the 240 seconds of the preceding 30-second default runs: 91,070 combination rounds, 112,955 component checks, and 91,070 learned clauses. Rows had 45 to 216 shared terms and 990 to 23,220 all-pair arrangements. EUF diagnostics reached tens of millions of disequality checks or pending-merge pops on several rows; solve time dominated millisecond-scale preprocessing.
counter_results.guided_eight_row_total: Seven rows made exactly 16 model decisions and then entered complete fallback; their guided phase performed 10,989 component checks before fallback. hash_sat_09_05 made no model decision or snapshot because LIA rejected all 4,330 complete Boolean models first. Care-pair counters were zero on every row.

profile_results.xs_7_7_default: 5000 rounds, 7064 component checks, 990 pairs and 2970 bridge clauses; 4.38 seconds, 15,356 KiB peak RSS. CaDiCaL propagation led at 24.84%, followed by SAT search and exact-rational tableau pivots/updates.
profile_results.xs_27_37_default: 1000 rounds, 1350 checks, 7750 pairs and 23,250 bridges; 5.30 seconds, 48,428 KiB. CaDiCaL search/propagation led; component extraction issued 31.8 million backend value queries and EUF rebuilt closure state.
profile_results.hash_sat_09_05_default: 3000 rounds/checks, each rejected by the first EUF component; 1653 pairs and 4959 bridges; 2.16 seconds, 18,668 KiB. CaDiCaL propagation was 49.23% of samples and component extraction issued 20.1 million value queries.
profile_results.medium12_default: 200 rounds and 400 checks, 23,220 pairs and 69,660 bridges, 93,640 SAT variables. The original run took 8.68 seconds and 124,692 KiB; the exact-command recheck took 4.23 seconds and 124,660 KiB. CaDiCaL propagation was respectively 35.38% and 20.54%; tableau update, violation maintenance, destruction, exact rational arithmetic, and copying dominated the rest. The wall-time variance prevents a local comparative-speed claim but leaves the structure, call counts, memory, and dominant mechanisms unchanged.
profile_results.certora_65782_default: 1500 rounds and 1571 checks, 12,090 pairs and 36,270 bridges, 50,193 SAT variables; 11.99 seconds, 70,696 KiB. CaDiCaL propagation was 82.91% and extraction issued 74.6 million backend value queries.
profile_results.hash_sat_09_05_guided: 1000 rounds/checks with zero pair materialization; 4.56 seconds, 13,340 KiB. Every assignment failed LIA before a model projection. Rational addition and LraTableau::check each took 16.84% of samples and pivots 10.53%, showing repeated full-tableau feasibility rather than combination scheduling.
profile_results.one_round_shape: At --max-theory-conflicts=1, medium12 complete versus guided created 93,640 versus 762 SAT variables, used 123,704 versus 9,704 KiB, and spent 209 versus 2.06 milliseconds in solve. Certora complete versus guided created 50,193 versus 1,904 variables, used 66,700 versus 11,216 KiB, and spent 164 versus 5.27 milliseconds. These are setup/shape diagnostics, not steady-state timing claims.

budget_probe_results.recoveries: At budget 256, xs_7_7 returned sat in 0.03 seconds with 32/990 pairs after 176 rounds; xs-15-09-3-5-5-3 returned sat in 1.84 seconds with 216/2926 pairs after 4630 rounds; xs-07-11-1-1-1-1 returned unsat in 0.14 seconds with 64/990 pairs after 792 rounds. None used complete fallback.
budget_probe_results.remaining: xs_27_37 remained unknown at 15 seconds without fallback after 126 decisions; xs_11_21 entered fallback after 86 decisions and remained unknown; hash_sat_09_05 still made no decisions; medium12 entered fallback at every tested budget through 256; Certora 65782 entered fallback at budget 64. Five of eight gaps therefore remain under these local bounds.
budget_probe_results.model_validation: Dolmen 0.10 directly accepted both satisfiable high-budget models: 2/2 pass, zero invalid model, timeout, read error, or solver error.
budget_probe_results.interpretation: The fixed default budget 16 prematurely triggers the quadratic fallback on three observed rows, but a higher fixed budget is not a general cure and has not been evaluated on SLURM or fuzzed. This result must not be used as a default-promotion or headline benchmark claim.

literature_review.primary_sources: de Moura and Bjorner, Model-based Theory Combination, Sections 4-5 and Appendix A; Bruttomesso et al., Delayed Theory Combination vs. Nelson-Oppen, Section 3; Jovanovic and Barrett, Sharing is Caring: Combination of Theories, care functions and EUF care graph; Bjorner and Nachmanson, Arithmetic Solving in Z3, Sections 4-5.
literature_review.highest_priority_gaps: Trail-synchronized DPLL(T^M) component state and partial-assignment theory layering; persistent/delta EUF and LIA contexts; a real QF_UFLIA EUF care-pair implementation; adaptive model-choice scheduling and live arithmetic model mutation; Int finite-domain/channeling preprocessing; and stronger explained partial-assignment propagation.
literature_review.secondary_gaps: Extended bounded GCD, stronger cube/bound reasoning, CDCL-integrated integer branches, broader Gomory cuts, cut selection, and HNF remain arithmetic gaps, but the watched profiles are dominated before these integer stages. The model-combination paper reports dynamic Ackermannization did not help its Wisa family, so it is not the first general remedy.

entries.evidence_status: local diagnostic profile and parameter classification only; exact source relation recorded; no algorithm or default changed; SLURM evaluation and fuzzing required before accepting any tuning
entries.outcome: The principal observed cost is repeated full-model orchestration: quadratic interface clauses burden CaDiCaL, every round scans all component atoms, and EUF/LIA state is rebuilt. Full incremental DPLL(T^M), persistent component contexts, EUF care pairs, and partial theory checks rank ahead of additional integer cuts for this watchlist. Raising the experimental model-decision budget avoids fallback and recovers three rows locally, but it is only a lead for a controlled SLURM/fuzz experiment.

entries.notes: Two predictions this run refuted, both recorded in the docs rather than quietly dropped. First, div/mod/abs were said to be rejected conforming input; QF_LIA and QF_UFLIA exclude those operators by name and readmit only * with concrete coefficients, so the original rejection was correct and Primo now accepts them as a documented extension. Second, supporting them was said to unblock the real-seed mutation gate; it moved the yield from about 25% to 22.8%, because typefuzz's mutants overwhelmingly carry non-constant divisors that are nonlinear whatever the frontend accepts. What the work does buy is usability plus the term kinds themselves, which removed the blocker that lead 16 named as its main design question. The net effect of the ite change on solved counts is NOT established: 824 files with answer equality detects a regression but does not measure the balance, and a full-division run is needed for that.

results.diagnosis: SUPERSEDED, see 2026-09-05-ite-loss-attribution-131983. This field read: '73 of 79 losses are timeouts rather than new incompleteness, and the median baseline solve time on them was 46.8s of the 60s budget with 42 of 79 above 45s. The cost is timeout-boundary churn from TermId order, concentrated in nec-smt where a large population sits within seconds of the limit.' The timeout facts are right and the attribution is wrong. It was never controlled: no noise floor was measured, and the 2.3:1 loss-to-gain ratio concentrated in the one ite-heavy family should have been the tell. A deterministic --preprocess-only comparison puts the preprocessed formula 10.11% larger on nec-smt and 0.00% different on almost every other family, matching a 10.23% paired runtime geometric mean on nec-smt against 0.99 elsewhere. Churn is real and large but it is not what the net number measured.
results.combination_layer: A QF_UFLRA probe with an ite spanning a UF application and an arithmetic atom gives identical :no.interface.terms, :no.interface.candidate-pairs and :no.purification.definitions on both binaries; head allocates 1 ite auxiliary where base allocates 2, because the repeated ite is hash-consed.

entries.notes: Conclusion: no capability regression and no soundness issue, but about 50 solves lost across the three divisions at a 60s budget. The earlier 824-file A/B reported 823 identical answers and was simply too small to see this; its own caveat said it could not measure the balance, and that was the load-bearing part. Two limits on the 300s reading: it covers only the 115 files that changed at 60s, so a file that got slower without crossing the threshold would not appear, bounded by the 0.5% total-runtime difference; and the per-file timing column in the QF_LRA and QF_UFLRA runs is unusable because bc is absent on the compute nodes, so only solved counts are reported for those.

entries.scope: Why the ite-as-a-term change lost 79 QF_LIA files. The 131646 entry recorded the loss as timeout-boundary churn from TermId order. This tests that against two things it never had: a re-reading of the timing data it already collected, and a deterministic measurement of the preprocessed formula size that no scheduler or timeout can affect.

Every other family: n=872, geometric mean 0.9878, median 1.0040, 664 of 872 within 5%, summed time -0.34%. Order churn does not concentrate on one family.

By family: nec-smt +10.11% over 2780 files; RWS -19.46% over 20; fft +4.61% over 9; 2019-ezsmt -0.01%; every other family exactly 0.00%.
results.auxiliaries: ite auxiliaries over the same files fell 2.75% (24969223 -> 24283101), and on nec-smt 2.74%. That was the metric the earlier 824-file A/B optimized and reported as the win.
results.conclusion: +10.11% formula size against a +10.23% runtime geometric mean on the same family is the same number twice. The losses are a deterministic encoding regression, not timeout churn: the equality distribution in simplify-extended-terms bought a 2.7% reduction in auxiliary constants for a 10% larger formula on the family that has the ites.
results.mechanism_probes: Same binary, one 16KB and one 1.6MB nec-smt file, (term-size.final / ite auxiliaries). Leaf off: 3505/314 and 453897/41415. Equality distribution off, rest of the leaf on: 3375/300 and 443718/40284. Default: 3747/295 and 489021/40264. Two rounds: 3677/248 and 561272/36344. Distribution off is best on both metrics at once, so the regression is that one rule and not the leaf.
results.fixed_point_is_exponential: Iterating the leaf to a fixed point rather than one pass reached 116s and 23GB on nec-smt/large/getoption_directories/prp-4-113.smt2, against 3.0s and 254MB with the leaf off, converging after 32 rounds. The single pass that looked like a missing fixed point was an accidental safety valve.
results.mechanism_confirmed: Why the rule loses on nec-smt and not elsewhere, measured on nec-smt/large/getoption_directories/prp-4-113.smt2: the distribution fires 18867 times and removes 20 auxiliaries (40284 -> 40264), for +58023 reachable nodes, i.e. 3.08 nodes per firing -- the guard structure and nothing more. nec-smt's ITEs are nested chains, so distributing (= u (ite c a (ite d e f))) removes the outer auxiliary and hands back (= u (ite d e f)), which needs one anyway. The benefit only arrives once the whole chain is distributed, which is what extra rounds buy and why they cost exponentially. Outside nec-smt the ITEs are single, the first firing is also the last, and the rule is a small win. This refutes the ancestor-rebuilding explanation first offered for the size growth: the per-firing cost is local and small, and the problem is that the rule fires ~940 times for every auxiliary it collects.

entries.notes: The noise-floor control this investigation was going to run (base against base under permuted declare-fun order, to size the churn band) was not needed: the deterministic size measurement settles the question without it, and 10172 byte-identical files show the change is inert wherever there is no ite. Two limits. The size metric is reachable-DAG node count after preprocessing, which is a proxy for what the SAT solver sees rather than a clause count, because --preprocess-only stops before clausification. And 79 files are excluded because preprocessing alone did not finish in 60s on either arm.
